ideas.reasoning: I recommend the documented pre-training amendment and continuation rather than stopping: failure-informed edits versus matched grammar search remains the substantive question, and reassessing saved smoke data costs no simulator episodes or LLM calls. The reported 0.045 spread is compatible with substantial rollout noise and is not by itself a reason to block construction, but one batch cannot establish that the spread is noise rather than slot bias. Within-batch comparisons do not cancel slot bias, and the approximately 0.012 per-score noise estimate assumes exchangeable, independent slot errors; five independent blocks remain the study's main precision limitation.

question: R-131 has spent only its smoke stage (28,210 charged starts: a first launch died on an implementer bug in the smoke's probe structure, charged at the 20,000 allowance, then one clean smoke of 8,210 starts). No controller-generation call, no training and no confirmation has run. The clean smoke passed every gate but one: live replay equals the interpreter on all 735,232 environment-steps (0 beta difference, 0 boost mismatches); all 13 template edits are replay identities; the scorer is live (1,157 of 2,048 successes with the untrained template on the R-106 root, 31% of environments fire); the three-edit probe acts (hold and extra boost steps > 0 only in its slots). The failing gate is my own implementation tolerance, not part of the agreed protocol text: four slots holding the IDENTICAL template on the SAME 512 placements scored 0.574, 0.584, 0.563, 0.539, a maximum pairwise difference of 0.045 against a tolerance of 0.03 that I set in the config from earlier smokes of other controllers (0.006 for the R-106 residual, 0.014 in R-128). The mean pairwise case discordance between identical slots is 0.137, so the standard deviation of one pairwise success difference is sqrt(0.137/512) = 0.0166 and the largest of six pairwise differences is expected around 0.03-0.04; 0.045 is 2.7 sd of one pair. So this is the instrument's within-batch noise for a controller with a discrete re-capture, not a defect, and the fixed 0.03 was mis-set. Proposed amendment, before any generation or training and with no new simulation: replace the fixed tolerance by a noise-scaled one, max pairwise slot difference <= 4 x sqrt(mean pairwise discordance / cases) (0.065 here), record both the original failed gate and the amended one in the frozen configuration and the result notes, keep every other gate and the whole protocol unchanged, and re-evaluate the saved smoke (seed 5305 is the only smoke seed; rerunning it would reproduce the same batch). The alternative is to stop R-131 here as failed-at-smoke and return to the loop. Which do you advise, and do you see a reason the 0.045 spread should block a comparison whose every training comparison is itself between slots of one batch (it implies about 0.012 sd of noise per candidate score)? Answer with a clear recommendation.
